feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope feels substantive. Impact is good, but the document is slightly overcrowded and repetitive, which dilutes the strongest achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong specialization in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for mission-driven organizations.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and visible career progression within NACo.  
- Writing is generally polished, professional, and consistent in tone; no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate to create a tighter, more executive-level CV.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope/volume: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, search improvement, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation/list style varies (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and video”); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and weaker than role-relevant content.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language like “leading” or “delivering” to sound more executive.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page website” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related capabilities and reducing the long list.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it broad here and save specifics for later sections.
- “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” already conveys much of the same positioning as the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad digital functions.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership”
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”; “Workflow automation and platform integrations” for consistency
- Consider prioritizing the most marketable/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or making it more distinct from those lists.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well established elsewhere in the CV.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the block is too dense and repeats points already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a clean heading and use concise, parallel one-line project summaries; e.g., “Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search; We Are Counties Microsite; Organization Anniversary Campaign; Advocacy Video Series.”
- Tighten wording: “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Standardize style and hyphenation: use “bill-level,” “multi-part,” and either “AI-enabled” throughout or another single preferred form.
- Consider adding one concrete outcome or scope where available, especially for the microsite or search project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current/past Work Experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” may also echo broader campaign/storytelling work unless framed as a distinct flagship project.

items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives to make this recent entry carry more weight.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations: “Built cross-channel workflows, analytics and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users, publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, or engagement gains from the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” overlap with the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new here: consulting scope, hands-on build work, and AI-enabled search.
- The Drupal microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the project section carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and add 1–2 results tied to channel growth, efficiency, or cost savings.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor achievement; compress supporting metrics into one line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen outcome language on analytics/governance: specify what improved if possible (e.g., reporting speed, adoption, publishing consistency, campaign decision-making).
- Add measurable impact for email/social/video/studio where possible: subscriber growth, engagement lift, production cost savings, faster turnaround, or number of events/programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” and recurring video/programming overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- “Governance/publishing standards” also echoes the current consulting role; emphasize NACo-specific scale and execution.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper outcomes and less generic “helped” phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and ownership: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Replace weak verbs: change “helping scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” to action/result language like “streamlined,” “standardized,” “launched,” or “institutionalized.”
- Combine related bullets for concision: newsletters + video + workflows can become 3 tighter bullets instead of 5.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: open/click rates, newsletter audience growth, video cadence/views, turnaround time, publishing volume, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the footer project and the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” echo the Director role; keep this entry focused on operational execution rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize strategic leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy and modernization
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “digital governance” if those are stronger differentiators in target roles.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep terminology consistent with recent experience: use “communications” rather than “messaging,” and “governance” rather than broader, vaguer phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/core competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress only if it is still relevant to target roles; your recent experience is much more Drupal-led.
- Replace “technical execution” with more outcome-oriented language if possible: “Web Platforms, Integrations & Automation” or “CMS Platforms & Digital Implementation.”
- If space allows, sharpen one item to impact: “AI-enabled search and structured content experiences” or “CMS modernization for high-volume public-facing sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership rather than repeating tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity).”
- Put business use before platforms: lead with “KPI design,” “executive/leadership reporting,” and “performance optimization.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” for clearer, more standard phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack here if those tools are already listed in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it sharper by emphasizing higher-value, recent capabilities and reducing tool-level phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- Multi-camera/PTZ production workflows
- Replace “PTZ camera systems” with “multi-camera/PTZ production workflows” to sound more strategic and less equipment-list-like.
- Consider dropping either “video production and editing” or “studio operations” if space is tight; the strongest recent differentiator is building and running an in-house studio.
- If you can support it elsewhere, tie this area to scale: recurring advocacy programming, conference/event delivery, or in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” may duplicate NACo experience unless this skills line adds a clearer specialization.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating names only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint** first, then secondary tools.
- Consider adding version/scope where strongest: **Drupal 10** or **enterprise/public-sector CMS environments**.
- Keep it platform-focused only; avoid adding implementation skills here since those already appear in Coding & Technical Implementation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus CMS modernization.
- If you keep both sections, make this one more specific to platform depth and let Topline Skills cover broader technical capability.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Use cleaner, current phrasing: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript” and move “jQuery” later to signal it’s secondary/legacy.
- Group by function for readability: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “custom front-end implementation,” “CMS troubleshooting,” or “deployment workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you specifically use it for technical implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a flat list to grouped systems: “Workflow automation & PM systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello; collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used to build editorial planning, approvals, cross-team coordination and reporting workflows.”
- Put the strongest, most differentiating tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira; move generic collaboration tools to the end.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and stronger alignment with recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating identical phrasing.
- Slack/Teams may be too generic unless other sections are trimmed.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of current email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, keep this item concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten content to: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add only the most relevant qualifier: Enterprise/member communications, newsletter operations, journey automation
- Consider moving Dynamics 365 first only if it reflects most recent hands-on use; otherwise order by strongest/recentest platform

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter scale or email leadership here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- “Engagement” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this entry tool-specific

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack, but this item largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a tool dump. Tighten it to emphasize analysis/optimization capability, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Optimization Tools
- Replace with: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • Experimentation reporting
- If you want to keep “A/B testing,” make it more concrete: Experiment design & performance analysis
- Consider dropping “Dashboarding” since Looker Studio/Power BI already imply it; use the space for a more specific capability or tool

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the broader capability list there and making this section tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating generic terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational team-building, early web/video execution, and any concrete scale or output.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer action + outcome: “Supported a major website refresh, improving the organization’s digital publishing foundation” or quantify if possible (pages migrated, traffic supported, launch timeline).
- Make multimedia more specific: “Produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update that expanded NACo’s in-house advocacy and member communications capacity.”
- Sharpen leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- Avoid repeating generic workflow language already used in later NACo entries unless you can show this role built the initial systems.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later multimedia/digital roles at NACo.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and first-of-its-kind impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the remaining clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, participating departments, or types of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer work; keep this entry higher-level and innovation/program-focused.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here unless this role truly owned it; save deeper multimedia detail for the later digital roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Make it more tool-specific and concise so it complements, rather than repeats, broader capability sections.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
- Tighten content to software/platforms only: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator
- If you want to keep workflow capability, make it more specific: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio systems • Podcast editing/production
- Consider adding only tools actually used recently or at leadership level; if applicable, swap generic phrases for named systems/platforms.
